details: Bitcoin (BTC) has maintained its position above $80,000 despite a rise in US annual inflation to 3.7% in September 2026 and a second consecutive week of net outflows totaling $228.58 million from spot Bitcoin ETFs. This resilience comes as US technology stocks also faced significant selling pressure. However, some analysts, like Bloomberg Intelligence strategist Mike McGlone, warn Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 if US stocks decline by 20%, citing broader macro risks. Conversely, bullish indicators suggest a potential rally towards $93,000, supported by a bull flag pattern and increasing whale accumulation, alongside rising stablecoin liquidity on Binance.
title: Bitcoin Holds $80K Amid Rising US Inflation & ETF Outflows, $10K Warning Issued

details: Ethereum's upcoming "Glamsterdam" upgrade is poised to significantly increase the network's gas limit. The Hoodi testnet is scheduled to activate the upgrade on October 26, raising the gas limit from 60 million to 200 million, a 3.3-fold increase, potentially enabling more transactions per block. The mainnet activation date is yet to be announced by client teams.
title: Ethereum's Glamsterdam Upgrade Aims for 3.3x Gas Limit Increase on Testnet

details: The crypto regulatory landscape saw several developments this week. USDC became the first e-money token to be classified as "significant" under Europe's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). A federal court denied a joint request by the CFTC and Gemini to vacate their January 2025 settlement. Additionally, the OCC documented banking restrictions on digital-asset businesses, and litigation over Illinois's crypto transaction tax is moving towards an expedited decision. An English court also ruled that Chinese law governs ownership claims over 61,000 seized Bitcoin.
title: Crypto Legal Landscape Shifts with MiCA, CFTC, and Tax Rulings

details: Cryptocurrency hardware wallet company Ledger is investigating an incident where approximately $90 million was drained from its devices. The hack is linked to hardware implants found in wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller, CryptoBilis, compromising funds before users even activated them. Ledger has asked resellers in the affected regions to halt sales while it investigates, emphasizing that its own infrastructure remains uncompromised.
title: Ledger Probes $90M Hardware Wallet Hack Via Tampered Reseller Devices
